label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Tolu, I’m actually the person you’re asking for. I wanted Medicine, I was offered Biology, and I’m now in Biology 100L in a federal university here in Lagos. So let me tell you how it has really been, without “transfer is a myth” or “just accept it and read hard.”

I scored 251 in JAMB 2025 and applied for Medicine and Surgery. When I checked the portal and saw Biology, I can’t even explain the kind of disappointment I felt. I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere, cried and didn’t eat. My mum kept telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for almost two months after that. I eventually had to beg her to stop because every time she said it, I felt like I had failed everybody. So when you say you’ve been crying since afternoon, I understand. It’s not just a course name on a portal when you’ve pictured your whole life around something else.

Now to the transfer gist, because this is where people confuse themselves.

What my own level adviser told us is that to be considered for transfer into MBBS after 100L, we need **at least a 4.5 CGPA out of 5.0**, and even that is not enough by itself: **there must also be space in Medicine**. She also said we must have met the Medicine requirements/cut-offs for JAMB and post-UTME. According to her, roughly six people were moved into MBBS from the whole faculty last year, and she thinks more than 40 people applied. Please note that this is what we were told in my own school; it is not a universal rule for every university.

So Kingsley saying transfer is a myth is not accurate, at least from what my adviser told us. But favour’s “just read hard in 100L” is also too simple. You can read hard and still not meet the CGPA. You can meet the CGPA and still be affected by limited space. And your JAMB/post-UTME results may also matter.

Your 268 is a good JAMB score, but I honestly cannot tell you that it qualifies you for transfer because I don’t know your school’s Medicine cut-off or your post-UTME score. You need to check **both**. Please don’t let anybody on a forum use your 268 to guarantee anything.

I’m also not coming here as a transfer success story, because I haven’t transferred. My CGPA after first semester is **4.31**, not 4.5. I’m still pushing, but I won’t lie and say it has been easy or that crossing is sure. This is exactly why I think nobody should accept Biology believing that Medicine is automatically waiting after one year.

As for 100L itself, the work is real. I’m doing BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and Maths are particularly dealing with people. Then there are practicals and the expenses that nobody really mentions when they’re advising you online. My lab coat was ₦6,500, my dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and I still paid separately for the practical manual. I’m not saying this to frighten you; I just want you to know that accepting Biology means entering an actual degree with its own workload, not spending one relaxed year beside the door of Medicine.

But is Biology a bad course? Honestly, no. That has been one of the surprising parts for me.

During our first Biology practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group actually fainted. I was fine, and I remember being so interested in what we were doing that it occurred to me that maybe I genuinely liked this thing, not just the idea of becoming a doctor. I’m now enjoying genetics and cell biology much more than I expected. I won’t pretend that it completely erases wanting Medicine, and not everybody will suddenly fall in love with Biology, but it also hasn’t felt like the useless punishment I initially thought it was.

One thing I would gently advise is this: **if you accept Biology, be at least somewhat prepared to finish Biology.** Don’t accept a course you know you will hate for four years purely because somebody told you transfer is common. Transfer may be real in your school, but until you confirm the requirements and eventually get approved, it is not yours yet.

On the other hand, rewriting is not automatically the foolish option either. If Medicine is truly what you want and you’re ready for another attempt, that is your choice. But “just rewrite” also needs honesty. Staying home is not as easy as people make it sound, and another JAMB does not come with a guarantee.

My secondary school classmate, Ifeoma, rejected a Pharmacy offer because she wanted to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she is still at home. Her story doesn’t mean the same thing will happen to you, or that everybody should accept any admission they get. It just taught me that both sides have risks. People can make accepting admission sound like settling, and they can make rewriting sound like a guaranteed victory. Neither one is guaranteed.

Also, sitting at home while your mates are posting matriculation pictures and moving on with their lives can be mentally hard. That doesn’t mean you shouldn’t rewrite if that is your decision; it just means you should prepare yourself properly and not choose it based on pride or panic.

Before your acceptance deadline, please go to your own faculty/department, and the admissions office if necessary, and ask for the exact position in **your school**. If you can go physically, even better. Ask them:

- Does your faculty actually consider transfers from Biology into MBBS after 100L?
- What exact CGPA is required?
- Must the applicant already meet the Medicine JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, and do your own scores qualify?
- How does the availability of space affect it?
- At what point are transfer applications considered, and what is the process?

Don’t rely only on students’ rumours, including my own experience. My adviser’s information may not match your school’s rules, and one neighbour’s successful transfer does not prove what will happen in your set.

There is also a personal question I had to ask myself, and I think it may help you too: **do you want Medicine itself, or do you mainly want to be called “doctor” because that is what your parents expect?** There’s no shame in admitting that family pressure is involved. But try to answer it honestly when you are alone, without your dad, your aunty or CampusGist talking inside your head. Medicine is a long and demanding path; Biology is also a real path. Neither choice should be made only to avoid disappointing people for a few months.

My honest bottom line is this: your dad is right that transfer may be possible, and your aunty is right that you could enter Biology and finish there. The decision depends on the confirmed rules in your school, whether you are genuinely willing to study Biology if transfer doesn’t happen, and whether you are mentally and practically prepared for another admission cycle if you rewrite.

Whatever you choose, Tolu, it is not the end of the world. Accepting Biology does not make you a failure, and rewriting does not mean you have wasted your life. Right now the portal news feels like a final judgement on your future, but it isn’t. Get the facts from your school first, breathe, and make the decision based on reality—not shame, fear or forum pressure.
